title: Orange, blue and a kite on two legs
label: Brand gallery
lede: Burger Chef’s first buildings had a diamond-shaped roof arch and a kite-shaped street sign.[^6] Few photographs of working restaurants are freely licensed. Here are four that are, and our own drawings.

archive.caption: Cars at a Burger Chef in Killeen, Texas.
archive.alt: Black and white photograph of two cars parked at a Burger Chef at night
archive.credit: Photo: John Lloyd, via [Wikimedia Commons](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:CarsatBurgerChef,Killeen,Texas,1967.jpg), CC BY 2.0.

archive.caption: A Burger Chef sign in Albuquerque, New Mexico, late in the chain’s life.
archive.alt: Tall neon roadside sign reading Burger Chef Hamburgers Shakes
archive.credit: Photo: John Margolies, Roadside America Photograph Archive, [Library of Congress](https://www.loc.gov/item/2017709772/). No known restrictions on publication; via Wikimedia Commons, public domain.

archive.caption: A former Burger Chef at 6132 Allisonville Road, Indianapolis, in use as a dental office.
archive.alt: Single-storey green brick building with a low pitched roof and an empty car park

archive.caption: A former Burger Chef, later a Hardee’s, at 3127 West Washington Street, Indianapolis.
archive.alt: Vacant restaurant building with a mansard roof and empty sign frames
